chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from Jarrah al-Mad'ini from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, fasting is not merely abstaining from food and drink.
Then he said: Maryam said, 'I have vowed a fast (sawm) to the Most Merciful,' meaning silence. So when you fast, guard your tongues, lower your gazes, do not quarrel, and do not envy one another.

He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) heard a woman cursing her female servant while she was fasting. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) called for food and said to her, 'Eat.' She said, 'I am fasting.' He said, 'How can you be fasting when you have cursed your servant? Indeed, fasting is not merely from food and drink.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between physical fasting and spiritual fasting in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *sawm al-lisan* (fasting of the tongue), elevating fasting from a physical ritual to a holistic ethical discipline. By linking Maryam’s vow of silence to the Prophet’s rebuke of a cursing woman, it underscores that verbal misconduct nullifies the spiritual essence of the fast, a concept central to the development of *adab al-siyam* (manners of fasting).
